A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original policy-learning simulations in Tables 2–3. Appendix A also reports fixed-policy estimation experiments in Figure 1.

after.justification: Retains the original simulations and adds the authors' policy-learning evaluation on French reemployment data in Figure 1. Appendix C includes the estimation experiments.

M1.justification: New Appendix E extends the procedure to simultaneous concept drift and identifiable covariate shift. It introduces target-environment covariates, density-ratio estimation, cross-fitting across two datasets, and a reweighted policy-value estimator. The original Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only synthetic Gaussian-reward data. v2 additionally evaluates French unemployment counseling data, with public/private program choices and binary six-month reemployment outcomes. Appendix E's covariate-shift extension is theoretical, without an accompanying experiment.

E2.justification: SNLN from Si et al. (2023) remains the sole evaluated comparator, including in the new real-data experiment. v2 identifies Kallus et al. (2022) as the source of the SNLN implementation; it does not add a separate baseline.

E3.justification: The new real-data experiment evaluates sample sizes from 10,000 to 20,000 at delta=0.05 and 0.1. The appendix's general test-data description also changes from one 10,000-point set to 100 such sets, although v1 already used 100 sets for its KL-sphere evaluation. This does not establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: The fixed-policy convergence diagnostic is revised: the third MSE panel changes its intermediate-sample-size trajectory between v1 Figure 1 and v2 Figure 2, while retaining the overall decreasing-error finding. The KL-sphere robustness experiment is unchanged, and no component ablation is added.

E5.justification: Tables 2–3 retain 50 and 20 repetitions and 95% confidence intervals; the fixed-policy estimation study retains 50 seeds. The new real-data figure uses the established 50-seed, 95%-interval reporting practice. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased repeated-run count is reported.

E6.justification: New Figure 1 reports higher robust values for the proposed policy than SNLN on the French data; at n=20,000 and delta=0.05, the plotted means are approximately 0.119 and 0.114. All 32 numerical value/interval pairs in Tables 2–3 are unchanged. The retained estimation figure's third-panel MSE trajectory also changes.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds a generalized target value, Assumption E.1, asymptotic-normality and regret Theorems E.2–E.3, and a proof sketch. Appendix B adds explicit smooth function classes and conditional-distribution smoothness Assumption B.1. The original proofs are retained in renumbered Appendices D and F.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions remain essentially unchanged. The conclusion changes identifiable-covariate-shift handling from future work to an extension supplied in Appendix E. Remark 4.7 also removes the qualification 'up to logarithmic factors' from its optimality claim without changing the original bounds.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly identifies choosing delta as a methodological limitation and explains the tradeoff between insufficient robustification and excessive conservatism. Appendix E specifies applicability to identifiable covariate shifts with a bounded density ratio. The original interpretation of SNLN's conservatism is retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code link for a working real-data example, identifies the processed-data source and SNLN implementation provenance, and expands the sieve/ERM documentation. The stated random forests, cubic splines, Nelder–Mead optimizer, three folds, 0.001 threshold, and hardware descriptions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Adds references to Behaghel et al. (2014), Kallus (2023), Sverdrup et al. (2020), and Van der Vaart (2000) for data, software, and regularity discussion. The related-work narrative and positioning against joint-shift methods and Mu et al. remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence remain. v2 moves notation from Section 1.3 to Appendix A, expands cross-fitting explanations, reorganizes the experimental narrative, and adds an Impact Statement. Affiliations, acknowledgments, and publication information are also updated.

P2.justification: The main paper and references change from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout, with reflowed algorithms and redesigned table headers. v2 adds the real-data Figure 1 and redraws the previous MSE figure as Figure 2 with visible scales on all panels. Its last two panel titles inconsistently use alpha instead of delta.

improvement.justification: The real-data comparison, code-access information, and explicit delta-selection limitation add useful evidence and transparency. However, new Appendix E omits the leading minus sign and exponential '-1' required by Lemma 2.3, and Theorem E.2 uses gamma=m/n where its target-sample average requires a variance factor of 1/gamma. These inconsistencies undermine the new extension as written, leaving no reliably assessable net quality improvement.
